text.label: Demo review: "Tallyo" is a fictional invoicing app; the screenshots and measurements are real, taken from the demo page
text.headline: Neither sign-up field has a label, and the password shows as [[plain text]]
text.lead: The page looks tidy, but the one task that matters, signing up, fails screen-reader and keyboard users and exposes the password on screen. Fix the form and the invisible focus first; the contrast and phone fixes are cheap and come next.
text.checksNote: Measured with inspect_ui.py on 3 screenshots: home at desktop 1280×800 and phone 390×844, pricing at desktop. The tick marks the target. Keyboard focus was checked by tabbing through both desktop pages.
text.lensesH: Accessibility, forms and responsiveness are the weakest lenses
text.lensesP: A score of 0–100 shows how well the interface handles each lens. Below 40 means big problems on the screens checked.
text.shotsP: Each numbered box is an issue from the table; click it to jump to its plan. Red boxes are critical or in the top 3.
text.screensH: The sign-up path breaks at the form, not at the landing
text.screensP: The main task from first visit to account, as checked on desktop and phone.
text.matrixH: {qw} quick wins with high impact and low effort
text.matrixP: Each dot is an issue from the table below. Black dots are fixes to the current UI; outlined red dots are rethinks that need a test.
text.opsH: {n} issues ranked by ICE, {crit} of them critical
text.opsP: ICE = impact × confidence × ease (each 1–10). Severity (1–4) says how bad an issue is; ICE says what to do first. The top three are highlighted.
text.nextP: Each has a hypothesis, a success metric and the cheapest way to check it.
text.planH: Full plan: all {n} fixes, with selectors and target values
text.planP: For every issue: why it is here, where it is (page, viewport, selector, screenshot), the current and target values, the steps, metric, effort and risk. The top three also list alternatives, an experiment with a threshold and a pre-mortem.
text.dataH: Confidence is fairly high: the measurements are direct, but there is no behaviour data
text.dataP: Every value comes from the page itself. Without analytics or session recordings, impact on sign-ups is estimated, and the state issue (#9) stays a hypothesis.
how: Checked the available sources and asked 4 skippable questions (2 skipped, assumptions noted).
Opened the home and pricing pages at desktop and phone width, ran inspect_ui.py for screenshots, element boxes, computed styles and automatic checks, and tabbed through both desktop pages.
Went through all 12 lenses; every finding is labelled observed or hypothesis and cites a WCAG criterion or heuristic where one applies.
Scored severity and ICE, compared alternatives for the top three, set thresholds and ran a pre-mortem; then wrote the same audit as a hands-off file for an AI agent.
text.footer: demo data: fictional product, real measurements of the demo page

kpis.l: keyboard stops with a visible focus
text elements below WCAG AA contrast

maturity.note: The pages look consistent at a glance, so the UI is Usable for a mouse user with good eyesight. It cannot be called Consistent until the form and keyboard basics work for everyone and the four button shapes become one.

screens.p: Two CTAs of equal weight plus the form
No labels; password shown as text

marks.note: social icons 18×18, footer links 14 px high

ops.t: Give the sign-up fields visible labels and the right types (the password shows as plain text)
Raise text contrast: 37 of 97 text elements fail WCAG AA
One primary action: "Get started" and "Book a demo" compete with the form
Stop the phone page scrolling sideways (feature strip is 1,096 px wide)
Bring back the keyboard focus ring (0 of 31 stops show focus) and add the page language
Enlarge phone tap targets (9 of 17 under 24 px) and name the menu button
Remove the pricing countdown that restarts on every page load
Replace "Submit" with a label that says what happens
Show a response after sign-up: validation, loading and success states
One button shape instead of four corner radii (4, 6, 12, 999 px)
Put spacing on an 8-point scale (13, 18, 22, 26, 37 px today)
Lift small text: footer, social and VAT note at 10–11 px, body 14 px / 1.3
Show the current page in the navigation
Test an email-first sign-up (password on the next step)

1.h: If both fields get visible labels and the right input types, screen-reader users can sign up and nobody sees their password on screen, because the fields will be announced and masked.
1.m: Sign-up form passes the automatic label check (2 of 2) and a screen-reader run-through
1.t: Fix in a branch, run inspect_ui.py and VoiceOver/NVDA once (≈30 min)

5.h: If focus is visible again, keyboard users can see where they are and finish sign-up, because every control will show a ring when tabbed to.
5.m: Keyboard stops with a visible focus (now 0 of 31)
5.t: Tab through home and pricing after the change; rerun the focus check

2.h: If secondary text uses #6b7280 instead of #a3a9b4, the subtitle and legal text become readable for low-vision users and in sunlight, without changing the look much.
2.t: Swap the two greys in style.css and rerun inspect_ui.py on 3 screens

1.why: Both fields use only a placeholder ("Email", "Password") and no label: the automatic check found 0 of 2 fields with an accessible name (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2). Both are type="text", so the password is shown on screen and phones show a text keyboard instead of an email one. The placeholder disappears as soon as people type.

change.tgt: <label for="email">Work email</label> and <label for="password">Password</label>, visible above each field
remove the placeholder, or #6b7280 if kept as a hint

steps: Add a visible <label> above each input in index.html and link it with for/id.
Change #email to type="email" autocomplete="email" and #password to type="password" autocomplete="new-password".
Style labels in .card: 14px/1.4, color.text, 6px gap to the field.
Run inspect_ui.py on the home page (labels must be 2 of 2) and check once with a screen reader.
1.metric: Fields with an accessible name: 2 of 2 (now 0 of 2)
1.risk: The card gets ≈40 px taller; check that the form still fits the first desktop screen (it ends at 52% of 800 px now).
alt: Floating labels inside the field: rejected, they shrink to tiny text and often fail contrast.
aria-label only: rejected, it fixes screen readers but sighted users still lose the hint after typing.
1.thr: Labels check 2 of 2, password masked, and a screen reader announces both fields correctly
1.pm: It shipped and nothing improved for screen-reader users because the visible label was added but not linked (for/id mismatch). The acceptance check runs the automatic label test, not just a visual look.
accept: `#email` and `#password` each have a visible label linked by for/id (inspect_ui.py: labels 2 of 2)
`#password` is type="password" and the typed text is masked
`#email` is type="email" with autocomplete="email"; the phone shows the email keyboard
Form still fits the first screen at 1280×800

2.why: inspect_ui.py found 37 of 97 text elements below WCAG AA (1.4.3). The worst: the hero subtitle #a3a9b4 on white = 2.36:1, the Terms/Privacy links #a3a9b4 on #f6f7fb = 2.21:1, "/mo per seat" 2.36:1, the VAT note #b8bec9 = 1.87:1, the feature strip and "No card needed" #8d94a1 = 3.05:1. All need 4.5:1.
steps: Add a muted-text token (--color-text-muted: #6b7280) to style.css.
Replace #a3a9b4, #8d94a1 and #b8bec9 for text with the token; keep the lighter greys only for borders and decoration.
Rerun inspect_ui.py on home (desktop, phone) and pricing; the contrast fails list should be empty except the CTA handled in #3.
2.metric: Text elements passing AA: 60 of 97 now, target 97 of 97
2.risk: The page looks a little heavier; keep the hierarchy by size and weight, not by paler grey.
alt: Darken only the subtitle: rejected, leaves 30+ failing elements in the footer, strip and pricing.
Switch to a darker brand grey #5d6472 (5.95:1): kept as an option if #6b7280 fails on new surfaces.
2.thr: 0 text elements below AA on the 3 checked screens (excluding text over images)
2.pm: It shipped and the check still failed because the greys were hard-coded in 6 places and two were missed. Search style.css for every hex value first and replace them through the token.

3.why: The hero has two filled buttons of the same size (Get started free 180×46, Book a demo 153×46) and the form beside it has a third filled button ("Submit"). The orange demo button draws the eye most (Hick's law, visual weight) and its white text is only 3.6:1 on #e8572a. On the phone both buttons sit side by side above the form.
steps: Make "Book a demo" a secondary (outline) button in color.primary.
Keep "Get started free" as the one filled button; on click, move focus to the email field.
On phone, stack the two buttons full width with the primary first.
Run a 5-second test with 5 people: what would you click first?
3.metric: Share of first clicks on the primary action (5-second / first-click test)
3.risk: Demo requests may drop; track them separately for 2 weeks.
copy: "Start free — no card": puts the cost answer into the button.
"Create my first invoice": names the outcome rather than the account.

4.why: At 390 px the page is 1,096 px wide: the feature strip uses five fixed 200 px items in a flex row with overflow: visible, so the whole page scrolls sideways and the browser can zoom out (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow).
steps: Set .strip { flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px 16px } and remove the fixed width from .strip span.
Check at 360, 390 and 820 px that nothing else overflows (inspect_ui.py prints SIDEWAYS SCROLL if it does).
4.metric: Page width at 390 px equals 390 px
4.risk: None worth noting; the strip becomes two or three lines on phones.

5.why: style.css has *:focus { outline: none } and no replacement: tabbing through home and pricing gave 0 of 31 stops with any visible change (WCAG 2.4.7). Keyboard users cannot see where they are. The page also has no <html lang>, so screen readers guess the language (3.1.1).
steps: Delete *:focus { outline: none }.
Add :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary); outline-offset: 2px } for links, buttons and inputs.
Add lang="en" to <html> on every page.
Rerun inspect_ui.py: focus visible must be 31 of 31.
5.metric: Keyboard stops with a visible focus: 31 of 31 (now 0)
5.risk: Mouse users see no ring with :focus-visible, so the look for them does not change.
alt: Box-shadow focus ring: equally valid; chosen outline because it survives Windows high-contrast mode.
Underline links on focus only: rejected, not enough for buttons and inputs.
5.thr: 31 of 31 stops show focus; a keyboard-only sign-up run-through succeeds
5.pm: It shipped and focus was still invisible on the blue Submit button because the ring was the same blue as the button. Use outline-offset so the ring sits on the white page around it.

6.why: On the phone 9 of 17 tap targets are under the 24×24 px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8): the 4 social icons are 18×18 and the 5 footer links 14 px high. Only 2 of 17 reach the comfortable 44×44. The menu button is 32×32 and has no accessible name (it reads as "☰").
steps: Give .social a and .burger width/height 44px with the icon centred.
Add padding to footer links so each is at least 24 px high and 8 px apart.
Add aria-label="Menu" and aria-expanded to the burger button.
Rerun inspect_ui.py at 390×844: targets ≥ 24 px must be 17 of 17.
6.metric: Phone tap targets ≥ 24 px: 17 of 17 (now 8); ≥ 44 px: at least 90%
6.risk: The footer grows by ≈30 px; fine.

7.why: The "Launch offer ends in 09:59" badge on pricing restarts from 10 minutes on every load: it is false urgency, a dark pattern that erodes trust and may break consumer-protection rules. Its text is also 4.09:1 on #fff1ec, below AA.

change.tgt: removed, or a real end date ("Launch price until 31 Jan")

steps: Remove the countdown script and the badge.
If there is a real launch price, show its real end date as plain text in color.text-muted.
7.metric: No fake urgency on the page; plan choice rate watched for 2 weeks
7.risk: A small drop in urgency-driven clicks, worth the trust.
copy: "Launch price until 31 January": true and still gives a reason to act.
"Prices locked for a year when you sign up now": a real benefit instead of a clock.

8.why: The sign-up button says "Submit", which says nothing about the result (Nielsen: match between system and real world). It sits under "Create your account".
steps: Change the button text.
Use the same verb in the success message ("Account created").
8.metric: Button names the outcome; first-click test on the form
copy: "Create free account": repeats the heading and the price promise.
"Start invoicing": names what people came for.

9.why: The form has no validation messages, no loading or disabled state on the button and no success message in the markup; the submit handler returns false. We did not submit it, so what users see after the click is a hypothesis: most likely nothing.

change.tgt: inline text under the field, linked with aria-describedby, after blur
redirect to onboarding or a confirmation message

steps: Submit the form once on a staging copy with a test email and record what happens.
Add inline errors for an invalid email and a short password, shown after the field loses focus.
Disable the button and change its text while the request runs; show success or a clear error.
9.metric: Every submit attempt ends in a visible success or a specific error
9.risk: Over-eager validation (on every keystroke) annoys people; validate on blur and on submit.

10.why: Computed border-radius across buttons: 12px (Get started), 999px (Book a demo), 4px (Submit, Log in), 6px (pricing Choose); cards add 8, 12 and 16px. Four button shapes on two pages read as four different components.
steps: Add radius tokens (radius.md 8px, radius.lg 12px) and use them in .btn, .login, .card, .plan.
Remove per-button radius overrides.
10.metric: Distinct button radii on the site: 1 (now 4)
10.risk: None; check the popular plan still stands out by its border, not its radius.

11.why: Computed paddings and gaps: header 13px 37px, card 26px 22px, strip 18px 37px, feature gap 22px, hero gap 48px. None share a scale, so edges do not line up between sections.
steps: Add a 4/8-based spacing scale as tokens.
Replace off-scale values; use one horizontal page padding (40px desktop, 16px phone).
11.risk: Small layout shifts; compare before/after screenshots.

12.why: 17 of 97 text elements across the 3 screenshots are under 12 px: social labels 10px, footer links and © 11px, the pricing VAT note 11px. Body text on the phone is 14px with line-height 1.3 (18.2px), tight for paragraphs.
steps: Set body to 16px/1.5 below 700 px and 15px/1.5 above.
Raise footer, social and VAT text to 13px.
12.metric: Text under 12 px: 0 (now 17 of 97 across the 3 screenshots)

13.why: On pricing.html the "Pricing" link looks the same as the others: nothing marks the current page and there is no aria-current (heuristic: visibility of system status).
steps: Add aria-current="page" to the active link on each page.
Style [aria-current=page] with color.text and a 2px underline.
13.metric: Every page marks its nav item

14.why: Asking for email and password at once on the landing is a common drop-off point; an email-first step can lower the effort of starting. We have no form analytics, so this is a hypothesis to test after #1 and #9.
steps: Add form-start and submit events to measure today's drop-off first.
Build an email-only first step behind a flag; password and name on step 2.
Run an A/B test for 2 weeks or until each variant has 300 sign-up starts.
14.risk: Two steps can feel longer; keep step 2 on the same page without reload.

answers.q: Which screens and task matter most?

answers.a: Skipped. Assumption: about half the visits are on phones, so both viewports were checked
No published tokens; keep the brand blue #3156d3
Skipped. Assumption: no user tests or complaints collected yet

WCAG.d: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines. Level AA is the usual legal target in the EU (EAA) and the US. Numbers like 1.4.3 are its success criteria.

AA.d: For contrast: normal text needs 4.5:1, large text (24 px, or 18.66 px bold) 3:1. #a3a9b4 on white is 2.36:1.

ICE.d: Impact × Confidence × Ease, each 1–10. The bigger the product, the sooner to do it.

inspect_ui.py.d: Part of this skill: opens the page at each viewport, saves screenshots, reads computed styles and runs the contrast, tap-target, label, focus and small-text checks.

tap target.d: The clickable size of a link or button. WCAG 2.5.8 asks for at least 24×24 px; 44×44 px is comfortable for a thumb.

Tap targets.d: The clickable size of links and buttons. WCAG 2.5.8 asks for at least 24×24 px; 44×44 px is comfortable for a thumb.

focus.d: The element that receives the keyboard. A visible focus ring shows keyboard users where they are (WCAG 2.4.7).

screen reader.g: software that reads the UI aloud
screen reader.d: VoiceOver, NVDA, TalkBack. It reads labels, roles and states; a field with only a placeholder is often announced as just "edit text".

CTA.d: The button that asks for the main action, here "Get started free".

Hick's law.d: The time to decide grows with the number of options of equal weight; two filled buttons plus a form make three.

dark pattern.d: A UI trick that pushes people against their interest: fake urgency, confirmshaming, pre-checked consent, hidden costs.

token.d: A named colour, size or spacing (color.text-muted = #6b7280) used instead of a hard-coded value, so one change updates the whole UI.

tokens.d: Named colours, sizes and spacing used instead of hard-coded values.

5-second test.d: Show the screen for 5 seconds and ask what it was about and what to click. Shows whether the hierarchy works.

pre-mortem.d: Imagine the fix shipped and nothing improved, and explain why. The reasons become checks you add up front.

A/B test.d: Half of the visitors see the new version, half the old; the difference shows the effect.

aria-current.d: An attribute that tells screen readers which link is the current page; also a hook for styling it.

Nielsen.d: Jakob Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics and 0–4 severity scale, the standard checklist for UI reviews.
